root_cause.text: In the NFC NCI core, `nci_close_device()` fails to complete pending data exchange transactions before device shutdown, leaving socket references held by the data exchange callback (e.g., `rawsock_data_exchange_complete`) unreleased, resulting in a socket memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks and calls to `nci_data_exchange_complete(ndev, NULL, ndev->cur_conn_id, -ENODEV)` when the `NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE` flag is set, along with ensuring `data_timer` deletion; the commit message states that the data exchange callback holds a socket reference and that pending exchanges must be completed on close to fix the leak.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the NFC NCI core, `nci_close_device()` fails to complete pending data exchange transactions before device shutdown, leaving socket references held by the data exchange callback (e.g., `rawsock_data_exchange_complete`) unreleased, resulting in a socket memory leak.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds explicit checks and calls to `nci_data_exchange_complete(ndev, NULL, ndev->cur_conn_id, -ENODEV)` when the `NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE` flag is set, along with ensuring `data_timer` deletion; the commit message states that the data exchange callback holds a socket reference and that pending exchanges must be completed on close to fix the leak.

candidates.rationale: Only flushes the command workqueue, leaving the data workqueue (which handles pending data exchange transactions) unflushed. Pending data exchange callbacks that hold socket references may still be in-flight, causing a socket memory leak.

Deletes the command timer without ensuring that any data exchange transaction that might have been scheduled by a timer callback is completed. If the timer was about to fire, it could start a new data exchange that holds a socket reference, leading to a leak.

Deletes the data timer without guaranteeing that pending data exchange transactions (which may be triggered by the timer) are completed. The callback of an ongoing data exchange may still hold a socket reference after the timer is deleted, preventing proper cleanup.

Releases the request lock without first ensuring all pending data exchange transactions are finished. This can allow the device to shut down while a data exchange callback still references a socket, leading to a memory leak.

Exits the function successfully without any wait or flush for pending data exchange transactions. Uncompleted transactions that hold socket references are abandoned, causing the socket memory leak described in the root cause.

Similar to the flush in hunk 0, only flushes the command workqueue. Leaves the data workqueue unflushed, so pending data exchange callbacks that hold socket references are not completed before device shutdown.

Deletes the command timer in a different code path (possibly an error path or alternative cleanup) without ensuring data exchange transactions are completed. This can leave socket references dangling.

Clears all flags except NCI_UNREG without verifying that no data exchange transactions are still pending. This premature flag setting can cause the device to be considered shut down while socket references are still held by incomplete callbacks.

According to the vulnerability root cause, this omission leads to a socket memory leak. No fix is present in this version.
